memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Say to the Levites: 'When you present the best part, it will be reckoned to you as the product of the threshing floor or the winepress. You and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere, for it is your wages for your work at the tent of meeting. By presenting the best part of it you will not be guilty in this matter; then you will not defile the holy offerings of the Israelites, and you will not die.'" — Num 18:30-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God closes these instructions with reassurance. Once the Levites had presented the best portion to the Lord, they were free to eat the rest anywhere, with a clear conscience. "You and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere... you will not be guilty." Having honoured God first, they could enjoy the remainder without shame.

There is real freedom in this order of things. When God comes first — when we give Him the best portion up front — the rest of what we have becomes ours to enjoy freely and without guilt. Putting God first does not leave us impoverished; it releases us to enjoy His gifts with a clear conscience. The priority of honouring God actually frees us to delight in His provision.

This overturns a common fear that giving to God leaves us with less to enjoy. In truth, giving God His portion first sanctifies all the rest. What remains is now enjoyed as a gift received from His hand, not clutched in anxiety. The one who honours God first eats their bread with gladness, not guilt.

This is the pattern of grace-filled living. We seek God's kingdom first, and everything else is given to us to enjoy in its proper place. Because Christ has secured our standing with God, we are free — free to give generously and free to enjoy His good gifts with thanksgiving. There is no anxious striving, no guilty hoarding, just the settled joy of a child who trusts the Father's provision. Put God first, and find yourself unburdened, enjoying His gifts with a grateful and untroubled heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you fear that giving to God leaves you with less to enjoy?
2. How does putting God first free you to enjoy His gifts without guilt?
3. What would it look like to live unburdened, trusting the Father's provision?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that when I honour You first, I am freed to enjoy Your gifts with a clear and grateful heart. Release me from anxious hoarding and guilty striving. Because of Christ, let me live unburdened in the joy of Your provision. Amen.
